# Aichi-source engine games: Regidrago attack-choice failure

**Agent 3, 15 October 2026.** Re-examined per-game action traces from the successful [manual Twinleaf run 38821042588](https://github.com/FlareZ123/experiment-01/actions/runs/38821042588), generated by [aichi-fixture.cjs](../../simulation/twinleaf/aichi-fixture.cjs) with pinned engine a9905a7 and unvalidated SimpleTacticsAi. All are tournament-source 60-card decks, seeded and 1200-action bounded.

| Source lists (engine seats) | Seed | Regidrago actions | Regidrago Prizes | Winner |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| Rank 1 Shadow Rider vs rank 10 Regidrago | 20261016 | Celestial Roar five times; Dragon Laser once; Apex Dragon zero | 0 | Shadow Rider |
| Rank 10 Regidrago vs rank 1 Shadow Rider | 20261016 | Celestial Roar three times; Apex Dragon zero | 0 | Shadow Rider |

In the first pairing, Regidrago's controller played two Regidrago VSTAR cards, but all six recorded attacks were used by a **Regidrago V**. In the reversed seating it played no VSTAR and only one Grass Energy from hand. As a control, rank-1 Shadow Rider mirror (seed 20261015) had five Latias ex Eon Blade attacks on one seat while the other seat recorded no attack at all. Hence the bot's issues extend beyond the Regidrago archetype.

The English card database identifies **Apex Dragon**, on Regidrago VSTAR SIT #136, as a Grass+Grass+Fire attack that copies an attack from a Dragon Pokémon in the discard pile. The upstream bot can perform some legal Regidrago V attacks while failing to exercise this primary VSTAR game plan. These traces do **not** establish whether the copy mechanism itself is accurate or broken, because it was never exercised.

**Actionable regression:** construct a replayable state with Regidrago VSTAR Active, the required Energy, and an appropriate discarded Dragon; ensure an Expanded-aware policy considers Apex Dragon and checks the copied effect against the advanced rulebook. Separately measure whether it chooses timely evolution and promotion when VSTAR is on Bench. Record attack identity, prizes, and turn order. Do not use Shadow Rider's wins here as a deck-strength ranking or projected 99.5% field result.
